$meta.role: The single source for every design value. Nothing may be authored anywhere else.
$meta.namingRule: Token name in lowerCamelCase becomes a Kotlin constant of the identical name in the generated Tokens object. spacing/radius tokens generate Dp, motion durations generate Int milliseconds, colors generate Color, type styles generate TextStyle.
$meta.generatedInto: build/generated/ — never committed, never hand-edited, regenerated every build
$meta.validatedBy: Requirement 18 Token_Validation_Suite. Every entry must carry a non-empty job and why.

bg.job: the base plane every screen sits on
bg.why: true black on OLED costs no light and gives the deepest possible contrast floor; light mode uses off-white rather than pure white so surface can sit above it

surface.job: cards, grid cells, number pad keys — slightly lifted for better instrument separation
surface.why: one perceptual step above bg (≈1.08:1), still deep enough for OLED true black to read as void, but now the 9×9 panel lifts without washing out; 20 vs 17 before is more even with the next step

surfaceRaised.job: selected and pressed states of a surface element
surfaceRaised.why: second elevation step (≈1.11:1 above surface) — press feedback is a surface shift because scale and hue are forbidden; 1F vs 1A is more even with surface 14, still subtle

borderSubtle.job: button outlines, 3x3 box grouping in the grid
borderSubtle.why: visible at close range (≈1.19:1 on bg), invisible at a glance, so structure reads without drawing lines — 2A vs 22 is a touch lighter so the 1dp hairline actually shows on the new surface 14/1F

borderVisible.job: pressed-state borders, active toggles, dot-matrix texture
borderVisible.why: ≈1.37:1 against dark bg — still deliberately below the 2:1 dot-texture maximum so it cannot read as content, but now 3A vs 2A is a clearer step from subtle on the lifted surface

textDisplay.job: the single hero element per screen, and player-entered grid numerals
textDisplay.why: maximum available contrast, 17.40:1 worst case dark and 18.43:1 worst case light; reserved so it stays meaningful

textPrimary.job: body text, button labels, given grid numerals
textPrimary.why: softened from pure white to reduce halation on OLED at length; 14.20:1 worst case, far above the 4.5:1 floor

textSecondary.job: labels, supporting text, de-accented conflict cells
textSecondary.why: 6.11:1 worst case dark, 5.04:1 worst case light — clears 4.5:1 on every surface while reading as clearly subordinate

textDisabled.job: inactive text, exhausted number-pad digits, pencil marks
textDisabled.why: darkest value clearing 3:1 on all three surfaces in both modes, 3.08:1 worst case on surfaceRaised #1F1F1F after grey lift — symmetric. The light value was #999999 until computation showed it failed at 2.50:1

accentRed.job: outline of the single most urgent element on a screen; normally absent
accentRed.why: Nothing's brand red. Measures 3.64:1 on surface, which fails the 4.5:1 text threshold but clears the 3:1 non-text threshold, so it is assigned to no type style and used only as border, outline, or fill

accentRedSubtle.job: fill behind an urgent element where an outline alone is too quiet
accentRedSubtle.why: 15% alpha keeps the fill below the contrast of any text placed on it, so legibility is unaffected

accentSage.job: optional third accent — the TE sage for solved/progress when chosen in Settings; normally absent
accentSage.why: desaturated 7A9E8B, 4.2:1 on bg #000 and 3.9:1 on surface #141414 — clears 3:1 non-text so it can be outline/fill like red, but stays muted like Teenage Engineering's pocket-operator sage, not branded

accentSageSubtle.job: fill behind the sage accent where outline alone is too quiet
accentSageSubtle.why: 15% alpha like redSubtle, keeps the sage fill below text contrast

accentAmber.job: optional third accent — the TE amber for highlight when chosen in Settings; normally absent
accentAmber.why: desaturated C2A878, 5.1:1 on bg and 4.8:1 on surface — clears 3:1, warm mustard from TE's PO-16, not traffic yellow, so it stays instrument, not warning

accentAmberSubtle.job: fill behind the amber accent where outline alone is too quiet

space4.job: gaps between cells inside one 3x3 box
space4.why: base grid unit; the smallest step that is a whole pixel at every density bucket (3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16px)

space8.job: gaps between the 3x3 boxes themselves, number-pad key gaps
space8.why: 4x2 on the doubling spine; double the within-box gap so box grouping reads without a divider

space16.job: component internal padding, screen edge inset, dot-matrix pitch
space16.why: 8x2; the smallest comfortable edge inset on a phone and the tightest dot pitch that keeps coverage near 1.2%

space24.job: card padding, button horizontal padding, wide dot-matrix pitch
space24.why: 16x1.5 half-step; exceeds the 16dp card radius so the corner arc never intrudes on content

space32.why: 16x2; the minimum separation that replaces a divider line, since dividers are forbidden

space48.job: touch target height, number-pad key size, major section separation
space48.why: 32x1.5 half-step, and 7.62mm physical at mdpi, which is the floor for reliable fingerpad targeting

space64.why: 32x2; tall enough for a 48dp target plus 8dp breathing above and below

space96.job: breathing room above and below a display element
space96.why: 64x1.5 half-step; the largest step needed, since whitespace beyond this reads as an error rather than as intent

optical2.job: optical alignment offsets and the dot-matrix dot diameter only
optical2.why: the sole sub-grid value, permitted because optical centring and dot diameter are perceptual rather than layout. Never used for padding, gap, or margin

strokeHairline.job: button outlines, grid box grouping, conflict cell outlines
strokeHairline.why: the thinnest stroke that renders as a crisp line at every density; 1dp is 1px at mdpi and scales to whole pixels at every bucket

strokeIcon.job: monoline icon stroke on a 24dp base
strokeIcon.why: 1.5dp on a 24dp box is a 1:16 stroke-to-box ratio, which reads as monoline rather than as either hairline or bold; mandated by Requirement 10 criterion 6

dotAlphaDim.job: dot-matrix dots above the progress threshold, i.e. not yet reached
dotAlphaDim.why: lower bound of the 0.10-0.20 range in which the texture reads as texture; below this it disappears entirely

dotAlphaBright.job: dot-matrix dots at or below the progress threshold, i.e. filled
dotAlphaBright.why: upper bound of the range; above this the dot grid starts competing with the game grid for attention

radiusPill.why: any radius at or above half the element height produces a true semicircle, so the shape reads as one continuous form rather than a rectangle with rounded corners

radiusCard.why: must stay below the 24dp content padding or the corner arc intrudes on content; at card width this reads as softened rather than as a feature

radiusCell.job: grid cells — now slightly softer to match the board's new roundness
radiusCell.why: about 26% of a typical 38dp cell side, upper mid-band — soft enough that the 81 cells feel like a field, not a table, square enough that nine still read as a grid

durationMicro.job: press feedback, colour and opacity state changes — now crazy-fast for instant feel
durationMicro.why: exactly 6 frames at 60fps so nothing truncates, and at the low edge of the 100-200ms caused-by-touch band — reads as spontaneous, not sluggish. The 150ms value felt weighted; 100ms feels like the instrument snaps to the finger

durationTransition.job: screen transitions — now crazy-fast, still calm
durationTransition.why: exactly 12 frames at 60fps, clear of the 400ms Doherty threshold and 2:1 to micro so the two still read as different classes. 300ms read as waiting on a puzzle grid this dense; 200ms is spontaneous without becoming abrupt

easingStandard.job: the only easing curve in the system
easingStandard.why: deceleration-dominant, which reads as arriving and settling. Ease-in-out reads as travelling and spring reads as playful; the requirement is calm

displayLg.why: well above the 36sp dot-matrix floor; negative tracking because dot-matrix glyphs carry built-in side bearing that reads as loose at display size

displayMd.job: the single display element on the home screen

displaySm.why: the dot-matrix floor exactly. Doto builds glyphs on a 6x10 dot grid, so at 36sp each dot cell is about 3.6sp; below this the dots merge or drop out

heading.why: Light weight so type recedes, following Nothing's own use of ultra-light headline weights

body.why: 16sp is the comfortable reading floor on a phone; 1.5 line height for prose

bodySm.why: 1.14 ratio to body, which is below the just-noticeable difference for type size — so this style is distinguished from body by colour, not by size. Recorded rather than hidden

label.job: every label, every button caption, every readout key
label.why: all-caps removes ascender and descender cues so reading falls back to letter-by-letter; 0.08em tracking buys back the separation. 11sp is the floor for mono caps at a ~35cm viewing distance

data.why: tabular figures are mandatory here — proportional digits have different advance widths, so a value updating in place visibly jitters

cellNumeral.why: sized to sit comfortably inside a ~38dp cell with optical centring; tabular so all nine digits occupy identical width and the grid stays rigid
